post.summary: Send a message, answer an approval or regenerate (useChat)
post.description:
The body is an AI SDK `useChat` request; the response is the UI message stream (`text/event-stream`).

- **Send**: the last message is a user message. Attachments are `file` parts (`data:` / `https:` URLs, or the `library:///uploads/…` url returned by `POST /library/files`).
- **Approvals**: when a turn ends with an `approval-requested` tool part, the client posts the assistant message back with the part in `approval-responded` (`addToolApprovalResponse` + `sendAutomaticallyWhen`). The continuation streams into the **same** message id.
- **Regenerate / edit**: `trigger: "regenerate-message"`, or a user message with `messageId`.

Busy policy: while a turn of this chat runs, a new user message is **steered** into it (`ifBusy=steer`, default): on this instance the response follows the running turn; when another instance runs it the message goes through the durable inbox and the route answers `202`. `ifBusy=reject` answers `409 EH_SESSION_BUSY` instead. Approvals, regenerate and edit never steer: `409`.

Errors after the turn started (model failure, stale approval answer) arrive as an `error` chunk inside the stream, not as an HTTP status.

get.description: Replays the chunks of the active turn from `from` and follows it until it ends, also when another instance runs it (stream log, ADR-0039). `204` when nothing streams: use the stored messages. A continuation turn after an approval replays only the continuation: refetch the message at the end.

post.summary: Answer an approval or a question
post.description:
`respond()` on the session that owns the item, from whichever instance receives the request. Nothing streams: the continuation runs server side (a child task continues, and when it ends the lead that waits for it resumes by itself) and shows in the events feed.

- Approval: `{ approved, reason?, note?, endTurn? }`. `note` is shown to the model after the result; `endTurn` ends the turn after the answer without a model call (`after-answers`, or `if-denied`).
- Question: `{ answers }` (one per question, `null` dismisses).

An item that is gone (answered elsewhere) is `404`; a stale answer or a running turn is `409`.

get.summary: Live event feed (SSE)
get.description: Every instance tails the `events` table (poll, 500 ms), so a client connected to instance B sees what instance A did. Starts after `after` (or `Last-Event-ID`); without either it starts at the current head (new events only).

schema.description: Server-sent events: `id` = seq, `event` = type, `data` = the JSON event. A comment line every 15 s keeps the connection open.

post.summary: Stop the running turn of a task (any instance)
post.description: `requestAbort()` on the task session: the instance that runs the turn stops it within one poll. A task that waits for an approval has no running turn (`target: idle`): answer or deny the approval instead.

post.summary: Send a message into the session of a task
post.description: Through the durable inbox (`enqueue`), so it reaches the instance that holds the session. `steer` joins the running turn at its next step boundary; `queue` runs after it. On an idle or finished task either starts a turn of the task agent. While approvals are pending the message waits behind them.

patch.description: Stored in the database and read by the agent factory of every instance: the agents are rebuilt on their next use, the budget limit applies to the shared ledger. `budgetUsd: null` removes the limit.

get.summary: List routines

post.description: A scheduled prompt for an agent. Every instance ticks; the one that wins the compare-and-set on `nextFireAt` fires the slot, once (`session.enqueue` with the deterministic id `sched:<id>:<slot>`). Missed fires after downtime are skipped (or the latest one fires within `catchUpWindowMs`); overlap defaults to `skip`. A fire that needs an approval lands in `GET /approvals` (needs action) and is never approved by the scheduler.

409.description: Archived agent or a schedule without a next slot

post.description: Recomputes the next slot from now (nothing missed while paused fires) and resets the failure counter.
A manual fire with the same enqueue path; the schedule is untouched. `409 ROUTINE_BUSY` when overlap is `skip` and the previous run is still in the way.
